mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is subject to epigenetic regulation and this regulation may play a significant role in cancer development.

the role of mtDNA‐associated mitoepigenetics in cancer, and the development of innovative strategies to reverse these aberrant epigenetic modifications.
the role of mitochondrial epigenetic modifications in cancer.

the mitochondrial epigenome, and the mitochondrial epigenetic machinery, are altered during carcinogenesis and that these alterations contribute to the development and progression of cancer.

mitochondrial DNA is not only a source of mutations, but it is also subject to epigenetic changes, which may have an important impact on the development of cancer.

the mitochondria are not merely the powerhouses of the cell, they are the guardians and the gatekeepers of the cell.

mitochondrial epigenetic mechanisms are involved in cancer development and progression and that these mechanisms can be exploited to design new therapeutic strategies.
